O.outcome_detail: Prospective within-individual self-concept effect on subsequent achievement

cells.quote:
In agreement with Marsh et al. (2024) and the reciprocal effects model, prior within-individual achievement had a positive effect on subsequent within-individual self-concept when adjusting for prior within-individual self-concept (b  = 0.119 [0.097; 0.141], p < 0.001) and vice versa (b = 0.146 [0.121; 0.171], p < 0.001).

However, contrary to Marsh et al.’s (2024) conclusion of consistent support for the reciprocal effects model, prior within-individual achievement had a negative effect on subsequent latent change in self-concept (b = −0.393 [−0.415; −0.372], p < 0.001) and vice versa (b  = −0.418 [−0.440; −0.395], p < 0.001).
cells.note: Both models were fitted to simulated data resembling the PALMA data; the contrasting signs show model-dependent prospective associations.

O.outcome_detail: Whether prospective self-concept-to-achievement effects are required

result.effect: RI-CLPM self-concept→achievement b = 0.146 [0.121; 0.171], p < 0.001; ESDM prospective effects absent

cells.quote: The ESDM (Fig. 1C) had a good fit (χ2 = 597, DF = 45, CFI = 0.977, TLI = 0.977, RMSEA = 0.059). This indicates that the data analyzed by Marsh et al. (2024) could have been generated by a model without any prospective effects between achievement and self-concept and, consequently, that the prospective effects they presented may have been spurious.
cells.note: The ESDM is not an experimental treatment; this is a comparison of alternative structural models fitted to simulated observational-data covariances.

O.outcome_detail: Prospective within-individual self-concept effect on subsequent achievement

cells.quote:
In agreement with Marsh et al. (2024) and the reciprocal effects model, prior within-individual achievement had a positive effect on subsequent within-individual self-concept when adjusting for prior within-individual self-concept (b  = 0.119 [0.097; 0.141], p < 0.001) and vice versa (b = 0.146 [0.121; 0.171], p < 0.001).

However, contrary to the self enhancement and reciprocal effects models, prior within-individual self-concept had no effect on subsequent within-individual achievement when adjusting for prior within-individual achievement (b = −0.004 [−0.053; 0.046], p = 0.880).
cells.note: The non-significant STARTS effect is coded ns, not zero, because no equivalence test or adequate-power claim is reported.

O.outcome_detail: Prospective effects in PALMA-like and TRAIN-like simulated data

result.effect: PALMA-like: RI-CLPM self-concept→achievement b = 0.146; LCSM b = −0.418; TRAIN-like: RI-CLPM b = 0.135; LCSM b = −0.128

cells.quote: For the four remaining models, findings were quite similar as in the previous analyses. The RI-CLPM suggested an increasing prospective effect of achievement on subsequent self-concept (b = 0.114 [0.085; 0.142], p < 0.001) and vice versa (b = 0.135 [0.109; 0.160], p < 0.001). The LCSM, on the other hand, suggested decreasing prospective effects (b = −0.106 [−0.130; −0.081], p < 0.001 and b = −0.128 [−0.153; −0.103], p < 0.001, respectively).
cells.note: This validation analysis used data simulated to resemble the TRAIN study; both datasets produced divergent prospective conclusions across models.

O.outcome_detail: goodness-of-fit of the victimization factor model

cells.quote: Both CFA and ESEM models identified the same three components (relational, verbal, and physical) for bullying and victimization responses. The difference between the two statistical approaches is that the ESEM models fit the data better, better differentiate the multiple components, and reveal the discriminant validity of the multiple components through the differential relations with critical antecedents and consequences of victimization.
cells.note: The study text reports this as a finding from Marsh et al. (2011); no numerical goodness-of-fit effect is printed in the supplied text.

O.outcome_detail: correlations among the three victimization components and their discriminant validity

result.effect: CFA correlations .81 to .84; ESEM correlations .43 to .52

cells.quote: Hence, their ESEM improved the goodness-of-fit and also resulted in systematically lower correlations among the three victimization components (correlations of .81 to .84 for CFA, .43 to .52 for ESEM). Both CFA and ESEM models identified the same three components (relational, verbal, and physical) for bullying and victimization responses.
cells.note: The lower ESEM correlations are interpreted in the study as better differentiation and support for discriminant validity; the reported finding concerns Marsh et al. (2011).

D.comparison: Sorjonen et al.'s specified latent change score model

O.outcome_detail: Model admissibility and reciprocal-effect estimates

cells.quote: We demonstrated (Núñez-Regueiro et al., 2025) that once these and other issues are corrected, the LCSM yields a proper solution (positive definitive variance-covariance matrix) and shows positive effects between ASC and ACH, consistent with the findings reported by Marsh et al. (2024).

D.comparison: Sorjonen et al.'s original STARTS specification

O.outcome_detail: Contemporaneous and lagged reciprocal-effect estimates

cells.quote: When the contemporaneous effects are introduced beginning on wave 2 (Núñez-Regueiro et al., 2025), the STARTS model shows positive contemporaneous effects of ACH on ASC, and positive lagged effects of ASC on ACH, consistent with the findings reported by Marsh et al. (2024).
cells.note: Model-specification comparison using longitudinal data; this is not an instructional intervention.

O.outcome_detail: Lagged ASC-to-ACH effect under temporal inversion

cells.quote: Results showed patterns of effect changes consistent with the inversion of causal direction in time-reversal testing: The positive lagged effects of ASC on ACH identified in Marsh et al. became smaller and was reversed in sign (negative effects) in the time-reversed variants, while the contemporaneous effects of ACH on ASC remained stable (Fig. 1B.2, C.2).
cells.note: The comparison used simulated data and the original PALMA data; the authors state that the pattern is compatible with, but does not establish, a causal interpretation.

O.outcome_detail: Model fit and probability of representing the true relations

cells.quote: This RI-LTVC had the second worst fit to the data compared to other models and a 0% probability of reflecting the true relations between ASC and ACH (Núñez-Regueiro et al., 2025), providing no support for a time-varying confounder explanation and indicating that the findings reported by Marsh et al. (2024) remain robust under this framework as well.
cells.note: This finding is reported from the authors' prior response and concerns model comparison, not an instructional treatment.
